entries.title: Who is a 'consumer'
entries.plain_en: A person who buys goods or hires services for their own use (not for resale or commercial purpose) is a consumer and can use this Act.

entries.title: 'Defect' in goods
entries.plain_en: Any fault, imperfection or shortcoming in the quality, quantity, potency, purity or standard of goods counts as a defect.

entries.title: 'Deficiency' in service
entries.plain_en: Any fault, shortcoming or inadequacy in how a service is performed (including negligence that causes loss) is a deficiency.

entries.title: District Commission: value limit and where to file
entries.plain_en: The District Consumer Commission hears complaints where the price paid for the goods/services is up to Rs 50 lakh (limit set by the 2021 Jurisdiction Rules). You can file where you live or work, where the seller does business, or where the problem arose.

entries.title: How a complaint is filed
entries.plain_en: A written complaint is filed before the District Commission. It can be filed online on the e-Jagriti portal (which replaced e-Daakhil from 1 Jan 2025).

entries.title: Time limit
entries.plain_en: File within 2 years from the date the problem (cause of action) arose. Late filing is allowed only if the Commission accepts a sufficient reason for delay.

entries.statute: National Consumer Helpline (Dept of Consumer Affairs)
entries.title: Free pre-litigation complaint
entries.plain_en: Before going to the Commission you can register a free complaint with the National Consumer Helpline on toll-free 1915 or consumerhelpline.gov.in; it tries to resolve it with the company.

entries.title: Deadline to pay wages
entries.plain_en: Monthly wages must be paid before the end of the 7th day of the next month. If you resigned, were removed, dismissed or retrenched, or the business closed, wages due must be paid within 2 working days.

entries.title: Claim for unpaid wages
entries.plain_en: The government appoints an authority to hear claims for unpaid or short-paid wages. A claim can be filed within 3 years from when it arose.

entries.title: New labour codes in force
entries.plain_en: From 21 November 2025 the Code on Wages, 2019 is in force and the Payment of Wages Act, 1936 stands repealed. Some state rules may still be in transition, so the exact office to approach can differ by state.

entries.title: Security deposit (MODEL law only)
entries.plain_en: The model law caps deposit at 2 months' rent (residential) and says it should be refunded when the tenant hands back possession, after lawful deductions. It applies ONLY if your state has adopted a law based on it. Otherwise your state's rent law and your rent agreement decide.

entries.title: Compensation for breach of contract
entries.plain_en: If the other side breaks the contract (e.g. the rent agreement's refund clause), you can claim compensation for the loss that naturally follows from the breach.

entries.title: Summary suit for money owed under a written contract
entries.plain_en: A faster civil suit route exists for recovering a fixed sum due under a written contract. Whether it fits your case needs a lawyer.

entries.title: Who gets free legal aid
entries.plain_en: Certain groups (e.g. women, children, SC/ST, persons with disability, industrial workmen, people below an income limit) can get a free lawyer and advice.

entries.title: Free legal aid helpline
entries.plain_en: Call toll-free 15100 for free legal advice, or visit the District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) at your district court complex. Applications can be made on plain paper.
